lines.cap: The richest man in the world got an envelope with his grandson's ear in it. And he still asked for a discount.
lines.say: The richest man in the world got an envelope with his grandson's ear in it. And he still asked for a discount.

lines.cap: J. Paul Getty. Oil billionaire. In the 1960s, he was called the richest man alive.
lines.say: J. Paul Getty. Oil billionaire. In the 1960s, he was called the richest man alive.

lines.cap: And so cheap, he put a coin-operated pay phone in his mansion, for his guests.
lines.say: And so cheap, he put a coin-operated pay phone in his mansion, for his guests.

lines.cap: In 1973, his sixteen year old grandson was kidnapped in Rome. The kidnappers wanted seventeen million dollars.
lines.say: In 1973, his sixteen year old grandson was kidnapped in Rome. The kidnappers wanted seventeen million dollars.

lines.cap: Getty said no. I have fourteen grandchildren, he said. If I pay one penny now, I'll have fourteen kidnapped grandchildren.
lines.say: Getty said no. I have fourteen grandchildren, he said. If I pay one penny now, I'll have fourteen kidnapped grandchildren.

lines.cap: Months later, a newspaper in Rome got an envelope. Inside was a lock of red hair. And an ear.
lines.say: Months later, a newspaper in Rome got an envelope. Inside was a lock of red hair. And an ear.

lines.cap: Getty finally paid. About two point nine million. Reportedly, only as much as he could deduct from his taxes. The rest, he lent to his son. At four percent interest.
